observation.body:
Legacy identity: `FOS-000006`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

6. **FOS-000006 — Stop replay-cache markers from certifying failed creation.** **S once `FOS-000005` exists; depends on `FOS-000005`; §2, §6.** [creation dispatch:1698](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1698) calls void creation routines, then calls `mark_replayed_resource()` for a recognized resource type regardless of Vulkan success. [marker:1196](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1196) also ignores its database write result. This is a source-confirmed path, not a reproduced real-driver failure. Write a successful-work marker only after the applicable creation/validation/output contract succeeds. Keep validation-whitelist meaning separate from successful compilation. **Check:** inject creation failure with no validation callback, rerun with the same replayer-cache and require the item to remain eligible. Test `--loop` and compile-required fallback so an eventual success is handled deliberately. Existing marker files lack stronger provenance; do not silently relabel their contents as verified reusable output.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Injected-creation and second-run integration tests:** A failed creation with no validation callback produces no successful-work marker; the next run attempts the item again. Verified success produces a marker only under its declared policy, and marker-write failure remains visible.
   - **Policy boundary tests:** Compile-required followed by successful fallback and repeated --loop attempts obey the documented final-item policy without double counting. Validation-whitelist entries and legacy markers are never presented as stronger success/persistence/reuse evidence than they establish.
